## TL;DR

Close-outs now validate up to `maxParallelValidations` queued jobs at once (default 2, range 1–8), while publishing to `main` stays strictly serial in queue order. Only the head of the pending queue may merge; a job that finishes validating early parks with its candidate intact until its turn. A job whose base moved is never published stale: real code drift sends it back through sync and the gate. `maxParallelValidations = 1` restores the old one-at-a-time pipeline. The change is covered by `src/server/__tests__/close-out-parallel.test.ts` (overlap, ordering, stale-base, failure isolation) and documented in `docs/close-out-pipeline.md`.

## Work and rationale

The scheduler is a pure function, `selectCloseOutStarts` in `src/server/integration-job.ts`, so the server's pump and the tests share one definition of the rules. It walks the pending queue in enqueue order, skips jobs that already have a live run, and stops at the concurrency limit. A job in `publishing` starts only when it holds the publish turn. The pressure guard holds only *extra* concurrency: the first run always starts, as before, and extra starts re-check every 30 seconds.

Per-run state (the owned attempt, the tasks a run stamped done) lives on `CloseOutOrchestrator`, so each run gets its own orchestrator through `processTask(taskId)` rather than sharing one instance. `server.ts` owns `pumpCloseOutJobs` and `runCloseOut`. The pump runs at enqueue, after every run's `finally`, and on the pressure timer, so a freed slot or a newly promoted head starts the next job at once.

Publish order is enforced in `processJob`. A job that reaches `publishing` while it is not the head returns `awaiting publish turn` and writes nothing, so its phase and attempt stay put. When it becomes the head, the pump restarts it. The publish turn also restarts that job's close-out budget (`budgetMonotonicStartNs`), so time spent parked does not count against `closeOut.timeoutMs`. The timeout check skips `publishing` for the same reason.

For stale bases I kept the existing guard rather than adding a cheaper re-merge. `publishCandidate` still compares `baseMainSha` with `main` under the repo and root locks. Bookkeeping-only drift publishes directly (`mainDriftIsBookkeepingOnly`, #0386). Any real code drift returns the job to `syncing`, so the candidate is rebuilt and re-gated, and the existing cap of five consecutive drift resyncs (`MAX_PUBLISH_DRIFT_RETRIES`) still applies. The task brief allowed a cheaper re-merge only if it could be proven safe, and I could not prove that without running the gate, so it fails closed.

The config key `maxParallelValidations` is in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, `loadConfig` (with the string-form fallback the other numeric keys have), `getConfigSchema()` as a select (Settings → General → Close-out via `settings-location.ts`), `SUPPORTED_TOML_KEYS`, and `user-docs/configuration.md`. The UI summary (`IntegrationPipelineSummary.vue`) shows parallel runs as "Also running" rather than queue position.

`queuePosition` now means publish order (0 is the next job to publish), which the API and driver brief both read. `phase` says what a job is doing. I made this call because overlapping `validating` jobs have no meaningful queue order, and changing `queuePosition` to validation order would have made the publish order invisible to callers.

## Approaches tried

The close-out lock that defers auto-reload is a run counter instead of a boolean, so it holds while any run is live. The advisory per-worktree check gate (#1061) is keyed per task, so it never serialises two different tasks; the publish step still takes `repoLock`/`rootLock`.

The brief allowed a cheaper re-merge for a moved base only if it could be proven safe. Skipping the gate for a re-merge is not provable in general, so real code drift re-runs sync and the gate. This is the fail-closed choice.

## Challenges and blockers

The first scoped `repoos check --changed main` in this session got through the build, format, lint, and contrast steps and failed in the tests step on one assertion: `decimal-number-fields.test.ts` keeps its own hardcoded table of numeric select settings and had not learned about `maxParallelValidations`. I added the row in the same order as `NUMERIC_SELECT_CONFIG_KEYS`. The scoped run is slow, so I ran it in the background and read its log.

The last scoped run also failed one unrelated test, `task-drawer-held.test.ts`. Its fixture hold date was `2030-01-01T00:00:00Z`, which renders as Dec 31 2029 on any machine west of UTC, so the year assertion failed here (America/Los_Angeles) and passed under `TZ=UTC`. The branch does not touch that file. I moved the fixture to `2030-06-15T12:00:00Z`, which keeps the year in every timezone, and changed the one raw-ISO assertion to match. It is a test-only change, and I'm reporting it so the reviewer can see it is outside the feature.

I also found a bug the tests had not caught. The UI snapshot numbered queued jobs `i + 1` over unstarted jobs only, so a job validating in parallel ahead of a queued one was skipped in the count, and "queue #" understated the real publish order. `queueDetail.position` now uses the job's index in the live list, which matches the API's `queuePosition`. In the serial case the numbers are unchanged. The existing snapshot test pinned the old value, so I updated it and added the blocker assertion.

Overlapping `git` writes to the candidate object store and ref namespace have not been load-tested. The docs say so, and a ref-lock collision would surface as that job's sync failing rather than as a stale publish. A human should run a multi-host close-out burst before relying on it at scale. I cannot prove that from this worktree.

Drift resyncs are more likely with overlap: a job queued far back can use up `MAX_PUBLISH_DRIFT_RETRIES` on a busy board. That failure is retryable and never publishes a stale candidate, but it is a real cost, and the docs say so.

## Key learnings

Splitting the scheduler rules into a pure function made the overlap, ordering, and held-start cases testable without spinning up the server. Keeping the stale-base guard exactly where it was meant the new code never had to reason about whether a candidate was current; it only had to decide who gets to reach that guard.

Phase and queue position need to be read together once jobs overlap. A `validating` job can sit at any position, and a `publishing` job that is not at position 0 is parked. Documenting this in one place (the close-out pipeline doc) was more useful than trying to make the number mean two things.
